title: research — multi-domain research with memory-first resolution and hardened verification
description: Use this when a question requires external discovery across one or more domains and the answer must be graded, cited, and persisted. A domain-neutral, expansion-first research process: it generalizes a question, resolves it from memory first (answering outright when memory fully knows it), and otherwise fans the question out across every domain it touches — routing each to a pluggable playbook (8 playbooks over 16 domains) via a structured sub-researcher prompt, so many domains are covered in parallel with the minimum number of dispatches. Findings are graded and written to memory; hardened verification proves the process ran on disk, in the memory store, and by recorded tool use rather than by self-report. An optional domain_narrowing input restricts the run to caller-named domains. Tool-agnostic: bodies reference capabilities, never tool names (ADR-0026).
author: sox-ecosystem

question.description: The research question, or a direction that implies one or more questions.

domain_narrowing.description: Optional. Restrict the run to this subset of the 16 domains; absent = all domains in play. The process still fans out across every allowed domain.

run_id.description: Run id; defaults to <ISO-date>-<slug>. Names the on-disk run directory under .research/runs/.

max_sub_researchers.description: Hard cap on concurrent dispatched sub-researchers (default 4). The parent also runs any single-playbook question inline.

run_dir.description: Path to .research/runs/<run_id>/ holding the verified evidence (manifest, questions, routing, findings, memory read-back, trace).

answer.description: Aggregated answer with confidence labels and citations.
